profile_text.body:
Modular, founded in 2022 and based in Los Altos, California, describes itself as providing "the unified AI inference stack from custom GPU kernels to production cloud serving on NVIDIA and AMD." The company's MAX Platform delivers what it characterizes as 2x performance and runs across GPUs, CPUs, and ASICs including NVIDIA, AMD, Trainium, TPU, Qualcomm, Intel, ARM, and Apple silicon. According to its site, the platform supports 1000+ models including DeepSeek and Kimi out of the box, with PyTorch-like model APIs designed for rapid model porting.

The company positions its core offering as a unified stack addressing fragmentation in AI infrastructure, replacing separate tools for serving, optimization, custom kernels, and scaling with a single system. Modular highlights portability across heterogeneous compute environments, enabling deployment from cloud to edge, and offers hosted cloud services as well as VPC deployment options with full-stack customization and performance tuning.

Modular's leadership draws from major technology infrastructure projects. Founder Chris Lattner previously worked on LLVM, Clang, MLIR, Cloud TPUs, and Swift at Apple, Google, SiFive, and Tesla. Other executives include Tim Davis, who led TensorFlow, XLA, and MLIR development at Google; Mostafa Elzoghby, former NVIDIA Engineering Director who developed cuDNN and CUTLASS; and Eric Johnson, who led TensorFlow API, Compiler, and Runtime teams at Google Brain. The company reports 220 lawsuits connected to California.
